title: Pack it like protobuf
hints: Each output byte carries 7 bits of the value: `value & 0x7F`. Then shift the value right by 7. The high bit `0x80` says "another byte follows", so it's set on every byte except the last.

Work out the length first (keep shifting a copy right by 7 until it's below `0x80`, counting bytes). If it's more than `cap`, return 0 without writing anything. Otherwise write exactly that many bytes.
`while (value >= 0x80) { buf[i++] = (uint8_t)((value & 0x7F) | 0x80); value >>= 7; } buf[i++] = (uint8_t)value; return i;` Note that 0 still takes one byte.
